title: rrt configuration
description: [tool.rrt] configuration for repo-release-tools. Place this schema URI in your TOML language server settings to enable IDE validation.

release_branch.description: Release branch name template. Use {version} as a placeholder.

changelog_file.description: Path to the changelog file relative to the project root.

changelog_workflow.description: How changelog entries are written. 'incremental' = append per commit; 'squash' = accumulate then promote on release.

tag_prefix.description: Prefix for this unit's release tags. Used as the default for 'rrt tag create/check --prefix' and to anchor the generated changelog range to the unit's own latest tag.

prerelease_base.description: Which core a pre-release channel (alpha, beta, rc) targets when started from a FINAL version. 'patch' (default): 1.0.0 -> 1.0.1-rc.1; 'minor': 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0-rc.1; 'major': 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0-rc.1; 'auto': level from Conventional Commits since the last FINAL tag (breaking -> major, feat -> minor, else patch). Advancing inside a channel (rc.1 -> rc.2) or switching channel (beta.2 -> rc.1) never changes the core. A version_groups entry overrides this global value.

version_scheme.description: The grammar the version is read, bumped and written in: 'semver' (1.2.3-rc.1), 'pep440' (1.2.3rc1) or 'calver' (2026.05.15). No default: when unset it is inferred from the primary target. A calendar-shaped version (YYYY.MM, YYYY.MM.DD or YYYY.M.D) is calver; otherwise a pep621 or python_version target is pep440, and any other target is semver. A version_groups entry overrides this global value. rrt bump --scheme and the MCP rrt_bump scheme parameter override both for one run.

post_policy.description: What happens when a post release (.post1) reaches a target whose format can't spell it (SemVer has none). 'refuse' (default): the bump errors, naming the offending target. 'patch': the whole group's bump is folded onto the next patch release instead. A version_groups entry overrides this global value.

changelog_paths.description: Git pathspecs limiting generated changelog entries to commits touching this unit's own files. Empty means no path filtering. Set per version group in multi-group repositories.

lock_command.description: Command to regenerate lockfiles after a version bump (e.g. ['uv', 'lock', '-U']).

generated_files.description: Paths to generated files that should be staged after a bump.

extra_branch_types.description: Additional branch type prefixes beyond the built-in set.

extra_commit_types.description: Additional conventional commit types recognized by rrt (e.g. ['security', 'ux']).

extra_section_map.description: Map extra commit types to changelog sections (e.g. {security = 'Fixed', ux = 'Changed'}).

pin_target_missing.description: Behavior when a pin target pattern has no match. Default: 'error'.

version_targets.description: Files whose version strings rrt will update on bump.

path.description: Path to the file containing the version string, relative to the project root.

kind.description: Well-known target type. Use 'pattern' with a 1-capture-group regex to read the version from a dependency pin or arbitrary string. All other kinds are mutually exclusive with 'pattern' and 'section'+'field'.

pattern.description: Regex pattern. When used with kind='pattern': exactly 1 capture group whose match is the version string. When used alone (no kind): exactly 3 capture groups (prefix)(version)(suffix). Mutually exclusive with standalone 'kind' and 'section'+'field'.

section.description: TOML table section containing the version field (e.g. 'package'). Must be paired with 'field'.

field.description: Key within 'section' that holds the version string. Must be paired with 'section'.

ci_format.description: Deprecated alias for 'format': 'pep440' -> format='pep440', 'semver_pre' -> format='semver'. Conflicts with an explicit 'format' that names a different value.

format.description: The spelling this target's version is rendered in (RRT-VER-1 tier 2). Unset defaults to 'python' for pep621 and python_version (SemVer spelling for finals and alpha/beta/rc, PEP 440 spelling for dev and post), 'rubygems' for gemspec and 'semver' for every other kind, so existing output is unchanged for finals and channel pre-releases.

pin_targets.description: Additional files kept in sync with the release version (e.g. CI action pins).

path.description: Path to the file containing the pin, relative to the project root.

format.description: The spelling this pin's version is rendered in (RRT-VER-1 tier 2). Unset defaults to 'semver', the spelling every pin has always received.

upstream.description: Upstream release source for `rrt sync` discovery.

commit_message.description: Commit message template for 'rrt sync --bump --commit'; {version} is substituted.

version_groups.description: Named release units for monorepo or multi-component projects.

prerelease_base.description: Per-group override of the global prerelease_base (patch, minor, major or auto).

version_scheme.description: Per-group override of the global version_scheme (semver, pep440 or calver). Unset everywhere, it is inferred from the group's primary target.

post_policy.description: Per-group override of the global post_policy (refuse or patch).

artifact_protection.description: Cross-pipeline artifact protection policy checked by the `rrt doctor` artifact-protection lens.

protected_refs.description: RESERVED, NOT YET ENFORCED: no check in `rrt doctor` currently reads this field. Setting it records intent only; it does not block anything from being deleted or flag any ref as protected.

consumed.description: Explicit declarations of artifacts consumed by another CI job, so a storage cleanup does not delete an artifact a different pipeline still depends on.

job.description: Part of the join key matched against a scanned CI fetch's (job, ref) — never job alone — by string equality (never split/normalized). On GitLab this is the real job name from the fetch URL's `?job=` parameter. On GitHub Actions, `actions/download-artifact` exposes no job identifier, so this must be the artifact's `name:` value instead; for a `run-id:`-without-`name:` fetch (download every artifact from the run), use the literal marker "*".

ref.description: Ref (branch/tag/run-id) the artifact is fetched from. Matched together with `job` as the join key — a match on `job` alone is not sufficient.

artifacts.description: Artifact-relative path(s) this job consumes. Must be replaced with real paths. When the scanned fetch's path is known (GitLab always sets it), the check requires that exact path to appear here, so an unedited TODO placeholder is caught. GitHub fetches never carry a path, so there the check cannot verify this field's contents and an unedited TODO placeholder loads successfully but protects nothing.

consumed_by.description: CI config file(s) that perform the fetch.

reason.description: Why this artifact must be protected.
